trait.description: Percent weight lost when frozen berries are thawed.

method.description: Remove frozen fruit samples the night before to fully thaw. Note the number of fruit per bag and weight to calculate average berry weight and percent drip loss. Carefully place the thawed fruit in a clamshell, separating it from the juice without squeezing the fruit, eliminating the release of excess juice or changing the fruit’s integrity. Weigh the juice. Calculate total drip loss as a percentage of fruit weight by the formula: W1-W2/W1 where W1 is the average berry weight before drip loss occurred and W2 is the average berry weight after drip loss.
method.reference: Mathey, M. M., et al. (2013). J Am Pomol Soc 67(4): 205-217.

trait.description: The total phenolic acids of fruit.

method.description: Total phenolics was measured on all fruit pulp samples by combining fruit and any juice lost during thawing in a zip top bag. Fruit was homogenized by rolling a weighted glass bottle over the bag, crushing the fruit and achenes. Homogenate was tested for titratable acid and then 1.5 mL was saved in three 2 mL tubes and stored at −80 °C. Thirty minutes prior to testing, one vial of each of the stored samples was thawed, vortexed and centrifuged. The determination of total phenolics was performed using the Folin-Ciocalteu method as described by Waterhouse (2002) modified for use in 90-well, flat-bottomed microplates (Greiner Bio-One, Monroe, NC, USA).
method.reference:
Waterhouse, A.L. 2002. Unit I 1.1: Polyphenolics:
Determination of total phenolics, p. 1–4.

method.description: Observe the plants and rate based on their flowering duration. Remontantcy is scored as follows: 1) flowering and fruiting only once in a season; 2) the potential to flower and fruit twice in a season, but strongly influenced by the environment; 3) flowering and fruiting twice in a season, largely irrespective of the environment; 4) flowering and fruiting multiple times, continuously in a season. Do not require decreasing day length for flower induction. In cases where stolons are observed, therefore, stolons produce flowers and fruits in the same season as the mother plant.
method.reference: UPOV TG/22/10 Rev. Strawberry, 2012-03-26

trait.description: Ferric reducing antioxidant power of fruit.

method.methodName: Ferric reducing antioxidant power FSH method
method.description: Measure FRAP using freshly prepared working FRAP solution (900 μl) and adding to 100 μl of standards or extracts. Standards curves using trolox (0–0.25 mM) and ferrous sulphate (0–0.5 mM) were run with each set of extracts and were linear within these ranges. Final result was expressed as ferrous sulphate heptahydrate (μmoles/g fruit).
method.reference: Benzie and Strain (1996, 1999)

trait.description: Ferric reducing antioxidant power of fruit.

method.methodName: Ferric reducing antioxidant power trolox method
method.description: Measure FRAP using freshly prepared working FRAP solution (900 μl) and adding to 100 μl of standards or extracts. Standards curves using trolox (0–0.25 mM) and ferrous sulphate (0–0.5 mM) were run with each set of extracts and were linear within these ranges. Final result was expressed as trolox equivalents (μmoles/g FW).
method.reference: Benzie and Strain (1996, 1999)

trait.description: The titratable acidity content of fruit.

method.description: Measure titratable acidity in 10 ml of juice diluted with distilled water (1:2 v/v) and titrated with 0.1 N NaOH, to pH 8.2, and expressed in mEq of NaOH per 100 g of fruit.
method.reference: Capocasa et al. 2008

trait.description: The firmness of fruit flesh.

method.description: Measure fruit firmness in grams using a hand-held penetrometer with a piston.
method.reference: Capocasa et al. 2008

trait.description: Skin color on the sun side of a fully ripe fruit.

method.methodName: Skin color chromameter reflect chroma index method
method.description: Measure color on two sides of 10 ripe undamaged and uniform fruit by using a chromameter, that includes chroma index, where a high chroma index indicates pale fruit and a low chroma index indicates dark fruit.
method.reference: Capocasa et al. 2008

trait.description: Skin color on the sun side of a fully ripe fruit.

method.methodName: Skin color chromameter reflect L* brightness method
method.description: Measure color on two sides of 10 ripe undamaged and uniform fruit by using a chromameter, that includes three parameters: L* (Luminance) a* (red tone) and b* (yellow tone) where L* is a measure of brightness.
method.reference: Capocasa et al. 2008

trait.description: The density of trichomes on the leaf surface.
